correctness.rationale: The proof treats every \(n\ge1\). First-round in/out degrees are \(F(P)=\sum_i(2^{s_i-1}-1)\) and \(\binom{k}{2}\). Merging block sizes \(a,b\) gives \(2(F(Q)-F(P))-1=(2^a-1)(2^b-1)\). The exact two-adic valuations for \(a<b\) and \(a=b\ge2\), together with a magnitude comparison and a separate \((1,1)\) case, show that this code uniquely determines the unordered pair. The second round sees every merged-pair type, and occurrences of a block size \(r\) in the pair multiset total \(m_r(k-1)\); \(k=1\) is unique. Symmetric-group transitivity proves orbit equality and stabilization. Distinct types \((1,1,3,3,3,3)\) and \((2,2,2,2,2,4)\) at size \(14\) share first-round degree pair \((15,12)\); adjoining singleton blocks yields counterexamples for every \(n\ge14\). Integer partitions for \(n\le13\) were exhaustively checked with a recursive enumerator. Direct full-graph and weighted-quotient programs corroborate, but do not replace, the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact, uniformly sharp two-round depth and the \(n=14\) first-round transition give structural logical invariants for a natural family with Bell-number-size vertex sets. The local coarsening-degree identity and injective two-adic encoding explain recovery of the entire global block-size profile. This is not simply classical type-orbit enumeration. The depth is independent of \(n\) and distinguishes the immediate-cover signature from the full-order presentation. The statement is deliberately restricted to the directed cover relation and includes publication-priority limitations.
